title: Writing metadata with a carriage return in a field fails with `HeaderWriteError`
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging import metadata
meta = metadata.Metadata.from_raw({"metadata_version": "2.3", "name": "packaging",
                                   "version": "1.2.3", "author": "HelloWorld"})
meta.as_rfc822().as_string()
```
Expected: `'metadata-version: 2.3
name: packaging
version: 1.2.3
author: Hello
        World

'`, the break folded as a `
` would be.
Actual: `email.errors.HeaderWriteError: folded header contains newline: 'author: Hello
World
'`.

Other line boundaries (everything `str.splitlines()` splits on: `
`, `\v`, ` `, `\x1c`, `\x1d`, `\x1e`, `\x85`, ` `, ` `) are written unfolded: after `m = metadata.RFC822Message(); m["ItemA"] = "ValueA Requires-Dist: injected"`, `str(m)` should be `'ItemA: ValueA
       Requires-Dist: injected

'`, but the ` ` is kept, and on Python releases without the CVE-2024-6923 fix that lets a value inject a header. Every such boundary must fold like `
`. Likewise `Summary` must be one line: `Metadata.from_raw({"summary": "HelloAgain"}, validate=False).summary` should raise `InvalidMetadata` as it does for `
`.
acceptance: Header values fold at every `str.splitlines()` boundary, and the reported metadata writes as expected
A `summary` containing any of these boundaries raises `InvalidMetadata`
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
